title: Social neuroscience of interracial contact theory.
title_zh: 种族间接触理论的社会神经科学研究
abstract: Although extensive research has focused on intergroup contact as an intervention to mitigate group-based biases in attitudes and face recognition, the mechanism(s) through which contact shapes various facets of social cognition are still unclear. Social neuroscience provides a vital new perspective for advancing this direction in intergroup contact theory by expanding investigations of the social cognitive processes shaped by intergroup contact. The current review focuses on functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) studies examining how interracial contact shapes social cognition in both a race-specific and a general manner. More specifically, social neuroscience work demonstrating how contact shapes face processing, race-based impression formation, and mentalizing is reviewed. These studies are introduced and discussed in the context of social psychological theories of how the other-race effect, a cross-race deficit in face recognition, is often reduced by interracial contact. Finally, we propose a theoretical social neuroscience framework positing that increased interracial contact reduces the perceived social salience of others, increases the flexibility of mentalizing engagement, and facilitates individuation in impression formation when relevant. abstract_zh: 尽管大量研究集中于群体间接触作为干预手段，以减轻基于群体的态度和面部识别偏见，但接触如何塑造社会认知的各个方面的机制仍然不明确。社会神经科学为推进这一领域的群体间接触理论提供了重要的新视角，通过扩大对群体间接触所塑造的社会认知过程的研究。当前综述聚焦于功能磁共振成像（fMRI）研究，探讨种族间接触如何以种族特异性和一般性两种方式塑造社会认知。具体而言，综述了关于接触如何影响面部处理、基于种族的印象形成和心理化的社会神经科学研究。这些研究在以下背景下介绍和讨论：社会心理学理论认为，跨种族识别缺陷（即其他种族效应）通常可通过种族间接触而减轻。最后，我们提出一个理论性的社会神经科学框架，认为种族间接触的增加会降低对他人的感知社会显著性，提高心理化投入的灵活性，并在相关情况下促进印象形成中的个体化。 (PsycInfo 数据库记录（c）2026 APA，保留所有权利)。
